source_text: Si quis dicit hominem perfectum assumptum esse a Christo, tanquam unum ex prophetis; et non confitetur ipsum incarnatione ex Virgine factum hominem, in Bethleem natum, et in Nazaret educatum, et qui progressum in aetate ostendit, et cursum temporum complevit; in Iordane baptizatus est, et a Patre testimonium hoc accepit: Hic est filius meus dilectus, sicut scriptum est; anathema sit. Qua ratione dici potest homo perfectus a Domino assumptus, tanquam unus ex prophetis; cum ipse Dominus per incarnationem ex Virgine homo factus sit? Ideo scriptum est: Primus homo ex terra terrenus. Postquam vero is, qui ex terra formatus erat, in terram abiit; secundus homo factus, in caelos ascendit. Et dicitur primus Adam, et novissimus Adam. Et sicut in confesso est, secundum ex primo esse, quantum ad carnem attinet; unde et homo, et filius hominis Christus: ita quoque testatum est, quod secundus sit Salvator primi, propter quem etiam e caelo descendit. Quoniam autem Verbum e caelo descendens, et homo factum in caelos ascendit; ideo et e caelo secundus Adam esse dicitur.
thought_title: Christ became man by incarnation, not by assuming a pre-existing perfect man
orientation: Gregory continues his series of anathemas, now condemning the view that Christ assumed a perfect human being like one of the prophets, rather than becoming man through incarnation from the Virgin.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says [a] man perfect [to be] assumed by Christ, as one from [the] prophets; and not confesses [him] by [the] incarnation from [a] Virgin made man, in Bethlehem born, and in Nazareth brought up, and who [having] advanced in age showed [himself], and [the] course of times completed; in [the] Jordan [he] was baptized, and from [the] Father testimony this received: This is [my] son [my] beloved, as [it] is written; [let him] be anathema. By what reason can [it] be said [a] man perfect by [the] Lord assumed, as one from [the] prophets; since [he] himself [the] Lord through [the] incarnation from [a] Virgin man made [himself] is? Therefore [it] is written: [The] first man from [the] earth earthly. After however he, who from [the] earth [was] formed, into [the] earth went; [the] second man made, into [the] heavens ascended. And [he] is called first Adam, and last Adam. And as in [what is] confessed [it] is, [the] second from [the] first to be, as to [the] flesh pertains; whence also [a] man, and [the] son of man Christ: so also [it] is testified, that [the] second [is] [the] Savior of [the] first, on account of whom also from [the] heaven he descended. Since moreover [the] Word from [the] heaven descending, and man made in [the] heavens ascended; therefore also from [the] heaven [the] second Adam to be is said.

choices.term: hominem perfectum assumptum esse a Christo
choices.english: a perfect man was assumed by Christ
choices.why: Literal rendering of the passive construction with 'a Christo' as agent; the error condemned is that Christ took up an already complete human being.
rejected: a perfect man was taken up by Christ

choices.why: Compares the assumed man to the prophets; 'ex' indicates source/origin.
rejected: as if one from the prophets

choices.form: ipse Dominus per incarnationem ex Virgine homo factus sit
choices.english: the Lord himself was made man by incarnation from the Virgin
choices.why: Reflects the causal/instrumental 'per incarnationem' and source 'ex Virgine'; 'factus sit' subjunctive in subordinate clause.
rejected: the Lord himself became man through incarnation from the Virgin
the Lord himself was made man by incarnation of the Virgin

choices.english: The first man from the earth, earthly
choices.why: Quotation from 1 Corinthians 15:47; 'terrenus' predicates the quality of the first man.
rejected: The first man is from the earth and earthly
The first man, from the earth, is earthly

choices.form: secundus homo factus, in caelos ascendit
choices.english: the second man made, ascended into the heavens
choices.why: 'factus' is participle modifying 'homo'; the second man (who was made) ascended.
rejected: the second man, having been made, ascended into heaven
the second man was made and ascended into the heavens

choices.form: secundum ex primo esse, quantum ad carnem attinet
choices.english: the second is from the first, as regards the flesh
choices.why: Literal sense of 'secundum ex primo esse' with limitation 'quantum ad carnem attinet'.
rejected: the second exists from the first, concerning the flesh
the second is from the first, as far as the flesh is concerned

bible_refs.note: Verbum e caelo descendens, et homo factum

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ assumed a perfect man, as one from the prophets, and does not confess that the Lord himself was made man by incarnation from the Virgin, born in Bethlehem, raised in Nazareth, and who showed his progress in age and fulfilled the course of time; was baptized in the Jordan, and received this testimony from the Father: "This is my beloved Son," as it is written; let him be anathema. For how can it be said that a perfect man was assumed by the Lord, as one from the prophets, when the Lord himself was made man by incarnation from the Virgin? Therefore it is written: "The first man from the earth, earthly" (1 Corinthians 15:47). After the one who was formed from the earth went to the earth, the second man, who was made, ascended into the heavens. And Scripture speaks of a first Adam and a last Adam (1 Corinthians 15:45). And just as it is acknowledged that the second is from the first, as regards the flesh; from which he is both man, and the Son of Man, Christ: so it is also testified that the second is the Savior of the first, for whose sake he also descended from heaven. Since the Word, descending from heaven, and made man, ascended into the heavens; therefore he is also said to be the second Adam from heaven.

problems.quote: And he is called the first Adam, and the last Adam
problems.source_quote: Et dicitur primus Adam, et novissimus Adam.
problems.why: Makes the second man ("he") both the first Adam and the last Adam; the Latin refers to two distinct figures spoken of in Scripture.
problems.fix: And Scripture speaks of a first Adam and a last Adam

edits.old: And he is called the first Adam, and the last Adam
edits.new: And Scripture speaks of a first Adam and a last Adam

fixed: Fixed mistranslation: source 'Et dicitur primus Adam, et novissimus Adam' speaks of two distinct figures, not one 'he' called both.

last_rejected.quote: the second man, who was made, ascended into the heavens.
last_rejected.source_quote: secundus homo factus, in caelos ascendit.
last_rejected.why: Splits 'homo factus' ('made man'), misrendering 'factus' as 'who was made' rather than 'having been made man' (or 'having become the second man').
last_rejected.fix: the second, having been made man, ascended into the heavens.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Secundus homo factus' follows 'factum hominem'; 'the second man, who was made' keeps the man-made sense without major loss.
